text: DRS-VPT localizes a single camera image inside a 3-D point cloud map, with no pose prior. One model works for driving LiDAR scans and indoor maps. It also calibrates a camera to a LiDAR without targets. Try it in your browser: upload a photo and a point cloud of the same place, and see the camera placed in the map. No install needed: DRS-VPT demo on Hugging Face . git clone https://github.com/ori-drs/drs-vpt.git && cd drs-vpt conda create -n drs_vpt python=3.12 -y && conda activate drs_vpt pip install torch==2.8.0 torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 pip install spconv-cu126 torch-scatter -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.8.0+cu128.html pip install -e " .[viz,dev] " pytest tests Linux, CPU only git clone https://github.com/ori-drs/drs-vpt.git && cd drs-vpt conda create -n drs_vpt python=3.12 -y && conda activate drs_vpt pip install torch==2.8.0 torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu # spconv-cu126 also runs on CPU; the plain spconv wheel is not thread-safe pip install spconv-cu126 torch-scatter -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.8.0+cpu.html pip install -e " .[viz,dev] " pytest tests macOS (CPU; builds the spconv copy in third_party/ ) xcode-select --install # C++ toolchain, once git clone https://github.com/ori-drs/drs-vpt.git && cd drs-vpt conda create -n drs_vpt python=3.12 -y && conda activate drs_vpt pip install torch torchvision pip install -e " .[viz,dev] " pip install -e third_party/ccimport --no-deps CPU_ONLY=1 pip install -e third_party/cumm CPU_ONLY=1 pip install -e third_party/spconv --no-build-isolation pip install torch-scatter --no-build-isolation pytest tests # the first run compiles spconv's C++ (about 30 s) The model weights (2.9 GB) and the demo samples download from the Hugging Face Hub on first use. python scripts/demo.py # KITTI sample with its K: prints the pose and its error python scripts/demo.py --predict-intrinsics # the same without K: the intrinsics are predicted python scripts/demo.py --sample 7scenes --viz3d # indoor sample, with a 3-D view python scripts/demo.py --sample iphone_stream # many frames against one map The figures are saved in demo_output/ . --viz3d-show opens the 3-D view interactively; --viz3d saves it, e.g. for the 7-Scenes sample (left: the query image; right: the map seen from behind the ground-truth camera, with the transformer's pose, the refined pose and the ground truth): Localize an image in a point cloud, or calibrate a camera to a LiDAR: the pose of the cloud in the camera. from drs_vpt . hub import load_model , load_sample from drs_vpt . inference import calibrate , read_image model = load_model ( device = "cuda" ) sample = load_sample ( "kitti" ) frame = sample [ "frames" ][ 0 ] image = read_image ( frame [ "img_path" ]) # (H, W, 3) uint8 RGB K = frame [ "K" ] # 3x3 intrinsics of the image cloud = sample [ "cloud" ] # (N, 3) float32 point cloud in metres grid_size = sample [ "grid_size" ] # voxel size in metres: 0.02 outdoors, 0.005-0.01 indoors out = calibrate ( model , [( image , K , cloud )], grid_size ) print ( out [ "T_cam_lidar" ]) # 4x4 cloud-to-camera: x_cam = R @ x_cloud + t out = calibrate ( model , [( image , None , cloud )], grid_size ) # without K: the intrinsics are predicted print ( out [ "T_cam_lidar" ]) QUICKSTART.md has the code map, the sample folder format and hardware notes. scripts/eval.py runs the released model on a test set and reports the paper's metrics: the rotation error (RRE, deg) and the camera-centre error (RTE, m), as mean and median, and the recall at RRE < 5° and RTE < 2 m. python scripts/eval.py --dataset kitti --data /data/kitti_vp2p_eval_data python scripts/eval.py --dataset nuscenes --data /data/nuscenes_test_processed/test python scripts/eval.py --dataset kitti --data /data/kitti_vp2p_eval_data --limit 20 # quick check Samples run 8 at a time on the GPU ( --batch-size ) while 8 processes ( --workers ) load and voxelize the next ones; lower --batch-size if the GPU runs out of memory. Each sample's result is written to eval_output/<dataset>/<name>.json (an interrupted run resumes), and the summary to eval_output/<dataset>/summary.json . The same evaluation from Python: from drs_vpt . eval import evaluate , kitti_samples , summarize from drs_vpt . hub import load_model model = load_model ( device = "cuda" ) results = evaluate ( model , kitti_samples ( "/data/kitti_vp2p_eval_data" ), out_dir = "eval_output/kitti" ) summarize ( results ) # {"n", "recall", "rre_mean_deg", "rre_median_deg", "rte_mean_m", "rte_median_m"} Data. Each scan is moved by a random rigid transform (up to ±10 m in x and z, any yaw), seeded with the sample index. KITTI (sequences 09 and 10, about 10 GB): python scripts/download_kitti_eval.py --out /data/kitti_vp2p_eval_data nuScenes: register at nuscenes.org , download v1.0-test_meta.tgz and v1.0-test_blobs.tgz into ~/Downloads/nuscenes , then: mkdir -p /raw/nuscenes/test for f in ~ /Downloads/nuscenes/v1.0-test_{meta,blobs}.tgz ; do tar -xzf " $f " -C /raw/nuscenes/test ; done conda create -n nuscenes python=3.8 -y conda run -n nuscenes pip install nuscenes-devkit opencv-python conda run -n nuscenes python data_processing/nuscenes_preprocess.py --dataroot /raw/nuscenes/test \ --version v1.0-test --frame_skip 2 --out /data/nuscenes_test_processed/test Results of the commands above with the released model, after the code refactor for this release. t and r are the mean / median translation and rotation errors; accuracy is the recall at 2 m / 5°. To localize many images in the same map, encode the map once with encode_map and localize each image against it, so each image only pays for the image side. from drs_vpt . hub import load_model , load_sample from drs_vpt . inference import encode_map , localize , read_image model = load_model ( device = "cuda" ) stream = load_sample ( "iphone_stream" ) # 37 frames in one map map_encoding = encode_map ( model , stream [ "cloud" ], stream [ "grid_size" ]) for frame in stream [ "frames" ]: out = localize ( model , read_image ( frame [ "img_path" ]), map_encoding , frame [ "K" ]) # K=None predicts it print ( out [ "T_w2c" ]) # 4x4 world-to-camera; out["K"]: the K used, at the model's resolution A video of DRS-VPT localizing and calibrating across driving and indoor scenes: calibrate also takes several synced image / scan pairs from a fixed camera and LiDAR, and solves for one extrinsic shared by all of them. On KITTI (sequence 09, after scripts/download_kitti_eval.py ): import numpy as np from drs_vpt . hub import load_model from drs_vpt . inference import calibrate , read_image model = load_model ( device = "cuda" ) kitti = "/data/kitti_vp2p_eval_data" sequence = f" { kitti } /sequences/09" # Intrinsics of the left colour camera, from KITTI's calibration file calib = {} for line in open ( f" { kitti } /calib/09/calib.txt" ): key , values = line . split ( ":" , 1 ) calib [ key ] = np . array ( values . split (), dtype = np . float64 ) K = calib [ "P2" ]. reshape ( 3 , 4 )[:, : 3 ] # Six synced image / LiDAR scan pairs frames = [] for i in range ( 6 ): image = read_image ( f" { sequence } /image_2/ { i :06d } .png" ) scan = np . fromfile ( f" { sequence } /velodyne/ { i :06d } .bin" , dtype = np . float32 ). reshape ( - 1 , 4 ) # x, y, z, intensity frames . append (( image , K , scan [:, : 3 ])) out = calibrate ( model , frames ) print ( out [ "T_cam_lidar" ]) # 4x4 LiDAR-to-camera: x_cam = R @ x_lidar + t DRS-VPT can also refine an existing calibration. On the Kimera-Multi dataset (Tian et al., 2023; a Clearpath Jackal with a Velodyne LiDAR and a RealSense D455), LiDAR points projected into the camera image with a starting extrinsic 1 (middle) and after refining it with DRS-VPT (right).
